subject: E2E region lockdown playbook and subprocessor evidence request (FinLytics procurement)
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@finlytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Residency guarantee + subprocessors for FinLytics evaluation

Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and legal asked me to confirm whether Redwood can provide a formal "region lock" option: specifically, that customer data for a pinned tenancy will remain resident in the chosen region (EU) except for an explicit, documented failover/DR event. They also want: the current subprocessors list, the jurisdiction of KMS keys used for encryption-at-rest, and any standard maximum duration for temporary cross-region egress in DR.

Two near-term asks from Procurement:
- A short playbook or bullet list describing how a failover would work operationally (who approves, how long, notice windows)
- Evidence artifacts for our security review (subprocessor roster, SOC2 report, dataflow diagram, KMS jurisdiction statement)

Can your team share a one-page playbook and the artifacts? Procurement reference: FL-POQ-2026-08. Timeline: they want signoff before 2026-08-20.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Infrastructure Security
FinLytics

Elena — appreciate the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can support a region-affinity offering with a documented conditional failover for DR, and we can provide the artifacts you listed.

Next steps I propose (quick):
1) Marissa: I’m looping you for commercial timeline and whether FinLytics prefers Hosted (with region-affinity SLA) vs Redwood Private (VPC) — both have slightly different contractual commitments.
2) Laura: please review legal artifacts and attach the DPA addendum/redline we’d want signed for the failover exception.
3) Aditya: can you draft the operational playbook (1 page) explaining approval, notification, max window, and technical controls (KV caching, transient egress logging)?

I’ll assemble everything into a single packet (playbook + subprocessors roster + SOC2 copy + KMS location statement) by EOD 2026-08-06 pending legal input. If procurement needs an accelerated timeline let me know.

Subject: Re: Residency guarantee + subprocessors for FinLytics evaluation

Elena / Ben —

Commercial quick note: we can offer a region-lock option as part of the Hosted contract with a region-affinity SLA (target: 99.9% affinity) and a contractual clause that permits a documented, limited-duration cross-region failover for DR. The Hosted path will include a signed DPA addendum; Private deployments have stronger contractual segregation but longer lead time and an integration fee.

A few clarifying Qs for Procurement so we size the commercial ask properly:
- Expected RTO for FinLytics failover? (e.g., 15m, 1h, 4h)
- Are you comfortable with a max monthly aggregate egress window (we typically see customers accept 1–4 hours/month for DR; we can tighten this in Private deployments)

If FinLytics is comfortable with up to 4 hours/month for DR with prior notice and a runbook-driven approval, we can proceed on the hosted contract path and provide a DPA addendum for signature.

I’ll work with Ben to include pricing for Hosted region-lock vs Private deployment in the PO. Targeting to have a pricing packet by 2026-08-07.

Marissa
Lead Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@finlytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Residency guarantee + subprocessors for FinLytics evaluation

Elena —

Thanks for the request. For clarity, here’s what Redwood considers "residency assurance" for the Hosted region-affinity product and the evidence we can provide immediately: 

Required evidence we will provide:
- Full current subprocessors roster (PDF) with process for notification of changes.
- SOC 2 Type II report (latest) — available under NDA / secure link.
- Short data flow diagram showing where ephemeral cross-region egress may occur (tech runbook).
- KMS jurisdiction statement: primary key material for hosted EU region is managed in EU KMS and keys are bound to the region (we will flag transient keys used for DR).
- Proposed DPA addendum language that limits cross-region failover to an agreed duration and requires prior notice (we'll attach a redline).

What we cannot contractually do on Hosted without Private: guarantee zero chance of transient cross-region egress in catastrophic operations — we instead offer a contractual cap and required approvals and full audit logging. For customers with zero cross-border tolerance we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or an on-prem package.

I am attaching a DPA addendum redline that defines: approval workflow (CSO sign-off + customer-approved runbook), maximum aggregate monthly egress, required notice period (48 hours preferred but can be shortened in urgent DR), and audit log retention requirements. Please review and let me know any redlines — we can move quickly on signature.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal
Redwood Inference

--

Laura / Ben —

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from Procurement/Legal:
1) FinLytics is willing to accept a maximum of 4 hours/month of aggregated temporary cross-region egress for DR if it is:
   - Pre-notified where feasible (we understand urgent DR exceptions exist)
   - Logged and auditable with immutable runbook entries
2) We will need confirmation that any subprocessor outside the EU will not receive customer plaintext data (i.e., processed in encrypted form or only for telemetry). Please include per-subprocessor processing purpose and data access levels in the roster.
3) For audit purposes, we will require a DocuSign or secure link for the SOC2 report and a statement of KMS key residency (which key IDs are bound to EU KMS).

Procurement reference: FL-POQ-2026-08 (attached). We aim to have a signed DPA addendum and PO by 2026-08-20 if legal review is complete.

Elena

FinLytics

- Evidence: we will provide (1) subprocessors roster with processing purposes and access levels, (2) SOC2 Type II secure link under NDA, (3) KMS jurisdiction statement with key IDs mapped to region, (4) 1-page operational playbook and runbook excerpt for approvals and logging.
- Contract: Laura’s DPA addendum redline is our starting point; we ask FinLytics legal to flag any specific contract language for redlines and we will respond within 48 business hours.
